newsitem.title: USA: Upstream oil and gas merger activity to pick up. [CORRECTED 23:56 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Upstream oil and gas merger activity to pick up. [CORRECTED 23:56 GMT]

text.p: Merger and acquisition activity in the upstream oil and gas sector is likely to intensify in coming months as majors seek to deploy their powerful balance sheets.
Earlier this week, one of the largest independent natural gas producers, Union Pacific Resources Group Inc made a hostile $4.0 billion offer for Pennzoil Co.
"You really end up with no choice other than to make a hostile offer if you identify value and are rebuffed by the board," said one investment banker, who declined to be named.

The upstream industry has seen already Australia's Ampolex fall to Mobil Corp in a hostile $1.4 billion bid aimed at gaining access to its acreage in the massive Gorgon field of Australia's NorthWest shelf.

"What the majors are after is not the proven reserves which is just the froth, it is the acreage that the targets hold which the majors have the financial muscle to exploit," said Fadel Gheit, analyst at Fahenstock & Co.
Potential takeover targets among the majors include ARCO, which has one of the poorer performance records among the major oils, and Occidental Petroleum Corp.
In the independent sector, Burlington Resources Inc is widely expected to be in the market for an acquisition before the end of the year.
"This industry has spent the last 10 years cleaning up its balance sheet, they have now done that and are casting around for synergies and potential acquisitions," said the banker.

He noted that although market tends to favour the defender in a hostile bid such as Pennzoil over Union Pacific due to the tangle of anti-takeover defences and litigation, the Pennzoil board will have to justify why it is turning down a potential $84 per share, 41 percent above the pre-bid price.
Since that bid was launched on Monday (corrects day from Tuesday), four lawsuits have been filed in Delaware.

Analysts say that bid may not be the knockout that Union Pacific had intended and depending on the value of the bidder's shares, which accounts for half of the offer, it could be worth $75 per share or $7.50 per barrel of reserves.
Other bankers believe that asset sales and friendly mergers will continue to provide the vast majority of deals.
Last month Amoco Corp said it would sell $2.5 billion disposal of domestic natural gas properties and the company says that its bankers have received a lot of interest.

"For sellers, there is a buouyant property maket and unless you see a big fall in energy prices, which we do not, the independents who can operate fields more efficiently," said Bob Munch head of CIBC Wood Gundy's global energy group.

The trend to friendly deals also took a new turn this week when Louis Dreyfus Natural Gas Corp and American Exploration Co merged and earlier this year, MESA Inc and Parker & Parsley said they would create the $3.0 billion Pioneer Natural Resources Co.
Both say their larger financial clout will enable them to ride the risky exploration business and bid for properties.
There has already been a large number of property sales in Canada, the Appalachian and MidContinent U.S., but one of the most attractive areas is the deep and shallow water of the Gulf of Mexico.
One deal on the cards there is between Ocean Energy Inc and an as yet unnamed major in the Gulf of Mexico.
"Everybody is looking at everybody else, we can expect to see more of this kind of activity," said Munch.
((-- David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
